title: Lecture 3 · Structural and binding roles of proteins

blocks.html:
What to know

  • Secondary structure is local. Alpha helices and beta sheets are held by backbone hydrogen bonds; they are the recurring building blocks of folded proteins.
  • Tertiary structure is the whole chain. Hydrophobic side chains cluster inside, polar side chains face water, and disulfide bonds, salt bridges, and hydrogen bonds lock the fold.
  • Quaternary structure is assembly. Hemoglobin is a tetramer of two alpha and two beta chains; binding oxygen to one subunit makes the others bind more easily (positive cooperativity).
  • Binding depends on shape and affinity. A ligand fits a pocket through several weak interactions; affinity is described by Kd, and a lower Kd means tighter binding.
  • Collagen and antibodies show the range. Collagen uses a repeated triple helix for tensile strength; antibodies use variable loops to recognize a vast range of antigens.

Check

check.question: Why does hemoglobin release more oxygen in exercising muscle?

options.text: Lower pH and higher CO₂ reduce oxygen affinity

check.explanation: The Bohr effect: higher CO₂ and lower pH stabilize the T state, so hemoglobin releases oxygen where it is needed.
